# @sharadox/sharadox-web-library

> Sharadox's own website library (verifiable source, not open source): content, branded components, styles and contact configuration for sharadox.com, built on the open-source @sharadox/*-web-library topic libraries.

- content/locale LOCALES (defineLocales en/pt); content/style STYLES (color group: black default, white, system; storageKey "style"); content/separator SEPARATOR "·"
- utility/separate separate(...parts) with the Sharadox separator
- action/send-contact sendContact(form, ip) — createContactAction to contact@sharadox.com, subject "Contact · Name (Company)", email or phone, at least one choice, 20+ character message, 5/hour per address, 50/day overall
- component/*: navigation, hero (+ lazy globe), service-index, about (+ feed), services (four groups of service-card, each with a service-object), capability, service-unlisted, marquee, process, faq, contact (+ form), footer, section-indicator, style-switch, structured-data, share-image (renderShareImage)
- style/token Sass helpers: tint, shade, dashed, on-scroll, below, fill-center
- License: Sharadox Verifiable Source License 0.1.0 (read and verify only)
- component/license License({ locale, markdown }) renders the license page body (marked); content/license LICENSE { path "/license", title, eyebrow, description }
- Navigation, Footer and LanguageSwitch take path? (e.g. "/license"): section links go to /<locale>#section, language links stay on the page; the footer links to the license page
- component/not-found NotFound({ locale, path }) the 404 screen (giant 404 with the live globe as the zero, failed request line, way home); content/not-found NOT_FOUND; ServiceIndex takes base? ("/<locale>" off the home page)
- content/slogan SLOGAN (with full stop) and SLOGAN_LINES; content/section SECTION { home, about, services, capabilities, process, faq, contact } with id + names; content/action ACTION.startProject; content/language LANGUAGE { label, names }. SITE.slogan, HERO.lines, HERO.primary, NAVIGATION.<name>, FOOTER.services/language, CAPABILITY.eyebrow and CONTACT.eyebrow were removed in 0.10.0 in favor of these.
- Language switch (internationalization-web-library 0.2): entrances skip on soft navigation (hero/not-found Motion initial, Sass mixin skip-entrance($durations...) for CSS entrances); site must render <LocaleTransitionStyle /> in <head>
- Service cards: SERVICES.items (groups web-application, mobile-application, creative, marketing; anchors; titled Web, Desktop & Mobile, Creative, Marketing) each with cards [{ key, title, text, action, chip }]; a card's key is its contact choice and its 3D object; ServiceCard's button links to #contact and calls requestContactNeeds([key]) (utility/contact-need, window event CONTACT_NEED_EVENT); ContactForm ticks the chip with a glow. CONTACT.needs.groups (chips grouped like the services) + other, and options (flat). Choices: website, platform, e-commerce, hosting, professional-email, progressive-web-application, android-application, ios-application, branding, rebranding, branding-design, print-design, merchandise, product-launch, lead-generation, sales-generation, brand-awareness, social-media-strategy, unsure, not-listed
- content/site FOUNDED 2026; the footer's copyright years come from CopyrightYears (@sharadox/time-web-library): "2026", then "2026–<current year>" as years pass
- utility/llms-text llmsText() → sharadox.com's llms.txt (shared shape from @sharadox/metadata-web-library). The cookie panel was removed in 0.14.0: the site stores only what it needs (language, style), which needs no consent.
- content/privacy PRIVACY (privacy-web-library options) and PRIVACY_PAGE { path "/privacy", title, eyebrow, description }; component/privacy-page PrivacyPage({ locale }); the footer links it
- 0.16.0: chevron icons from @sharadox/icon-web-library replace every text arrow (button, footer Back to top, 404)
- 0.17.0: component/consent Consent back (consent-web-library 0.3, required only: Got It and Details); footer: Cookie Preferences, Livro de Reclamações link and the CIMAAL consumer dispute notice (legal-web-library); privacy policy mentions the consent record
- 0.18.0: navigation links include One System (touchpoints); below 1100px a menu button opens the links and Start a Project under the bar, in the bar's frosted background, scrolling when it doesn't fit (Escape, a link or a wider screen closes it); footer Studio column adds One System and Start a Project
- 0.19.0: the globe floats (slow rise, fall and sway; still with reduced motion), in the hero and the 404; footer reorganized (brand, services, studio with Start a Project, language and style; wordmark; a bar with license, privacy, cookie preferences, complaints book and Back to top; copyright beside the dispute notice); the phone menu uses @sharadox/menu-web-library (any tap on a link or button in the bar or menu closes it, the logo included)
- 0.20.0: "What we do" is now Services: four groups (Web Applications: websites, platforms, e-commerce; Mobile Applications: Android, iOS, PWAs; Creative: branding, rebranding, branding design; Marketing: product launches, lead generation, sales generation, brand awareness, social media growth strategy) of cards, each with its own animated CSS 3D object (component/service-object, Cuboid primitive, style/object helpers) that turns towards the pointer (useTilt on the card), a description and a button that ticks its contact choice; contact chips grouped by service (component/contact/form/chip); service-action, services/cell and the old visuals removed; footer: no big wordmark, Start a Project is a solid button, everything legal in one section (title, copyright, links, dispute notice, Back to top); the process line fills as you scroll on phones too (--drawn); ServiceIndex has four cells and a chevron icon; structured data offers one service per card
- 0.20.1: same as 0.20.0, published again (0.20.0's npm publish failed at the provenance log)
- 0.21.0: Services: Web Applications adds Content Management Systems (CMS) and APIs; Mobile Applications becomes Desktop and Mobile Applications with one PWA card (wide, numbered points: no store in between, one codebase for every platform, less to pay and wait; its object sends one codebase to a computer, a tablet and a phone); Creative becomes Creative Services with plain-language descriptions of branding, branding design and rebranding; Marketing becomes Marketing Campaigns; a new social media object (feed, likes, posting calendar, followers chart); new CMS and API objects; ServiceUnlisted ("Didn't find what you were looking for?", ticks "not-listed"). Contact form: phone field under email (email or phone or both), chips "I don't know what I need" and "What I need is not listed" replace "Others", checks before sending (utility/contact-problem: name, email or phone, a choice, 20+ characters) with messages under each field; sendContact applies the same rules (form-web-library 0.3.0: requireChoice, minimumMessageLength) and the daily cap of 50 emails. Footer: the legal row sits on the same columns as above (copyright, links and dispute notice, Back to top), without the Legal label or dots. Organization logo is /profile-picture.png
- 0.22.0: Creative Services adds Print Design (business cards, flyers, brochures, menus, posters, stickers; object: a business card flipping off its stack in front of a flyer) and Merchandise (T-shirts, hoodies, caps, bottles, mugs, tote bags; object: a branded T-shirt beside a turning bottle), each with its contact choice; 16 cards in all
- 0.23.0: footer in four columns only: the legal links, the consumer dispute notice and the copyright sit under the brand (behind a dashed line, at the foot of the column), and Back to top under the style switch, level with the copyright; the separate legal row is gone
- 0.24.0: Merchandise removed from Creative Services (15 cards); internal links are Next.js links (SectionLink from scroll-web-library for sections, including the menu's animated ones, service index, section indicator, capabilities and footer; Link for the wordmark, license and privacy; Button picks for itself); email stays a plain <a>
- 0.25.0: Creative Services descriptions rewritten in plain words (branding, rebranding, branding design, print design); a group of two cards shares a row in halves and four make two rows of two, so no row is left half empty
- 0.26.0: Services renamed Web, Desktop & Mobile, Creative and Marketing. Web drops CMS and APIs and adds Professional Emails (object: an envelope opening behind an address that changes name, always @yourdomain.com); Platforms reads as your company's own system. Creative brings Merchandise back (designed by us, made by trusted partners) and every description is short, like the web ones; new objects: Branding (pieces of the brand settle on a board, then its mark rises), Rebranding (a divider sweeps the dated mark into the fresh one), Branding Design (a pointer drags a vector anchor and its handles, SVG with a still copy for reduced motion). Marketing cards are named campaigns (Product Launch, Lead Generation, Sales Generation, Brand Awareness Campaigns). "Didn't find the service you were looking for?"; 15 cards in all
- 0.27.0: New objects: Platforms (a company's people around one system, joined to it by lines; messages travel from person to person through it, its gear turning and its tasks ticking off; text: your company's way of working, made digital), Product Launch (a countdown over a covered product, then the cover lifts, the product rises into the light and sparks fly), Brand Awareness (a billboard, then word of mouth spreads the brand's mark through a crowd until everyone thinks of it together). Shared Person and Mark pieces (component/service-object/person, /mark); Branding uses Mark. animation-web-library ^0.2.3 (the marquee glides sideways). The 0.26.0 note above said 16 cards: there are 15
- 0.28.0: Web adds Hosting before Professional Emails (we host what we build, look after it and bring it back up if anything goes wrong; object: a server rack watched by an uptime line, one server has an incident, goes dark, and comes back with a tick); Web is now three cards over two. Desktop & Mobile brings back Android Applications and iOS Applications after the PWA (three cards in a row; the PWA card is short like the others, without its points; lead "Apps for every screen."). New Product Launch object: a campaign timeline lighting step by step (teaser, landing page, campaign, launch day with the product revealed and confetti). ServiceCard has no `wide` or `points` any more. 18 cards in all
- 0.29.0: Hosting's object is only the server rack (no uptime line): one server goes dark and comes back with a tick. Android's object looks like Android (camera hole, round icons, search bar, three buttons, the quick settings shade sliding down and its toggles switching on); iOS's like an iPhone (Dynamic Island opening into a live activity, rounded-square icons that jiggle, page dots, dock, home bar). Product Launch is a 3-2-1 countdown, each number flowing smoothly into the next inside a ring that runs out, then a rocket lifts off with flame, smoke and a trail
- 0.30.0: Product Launch is in 3D: a round rocket (eight shaded panels, a nose cone of eight leaning panels, four fins, a window) turning slowly on a 3D pad, the flame as two crossed sheets, smoke rolling out all around the pad; the countdown floats in front. scroll-web-library ^0.4.2 (a glide never carries over to the next page)
- 0.31.0: One palette for every 3D object (style/object: surface(), $surface, $raised, $edge, $hint, $faint, $detail, $strong, $glow; face() is opaque; Cuboid faces opaque), so they match in Black and White. Hosting: only the rack (no tick). Branding: the brand's identity card filling in (mark, name, audience, voice, colors, type), then lifting. Rebranding: the dated badge turns and reshapes into the fresh diamond, and the change rolls out to a business card and an app icon. Branding Design: the pointer drags the top anchor of a round shape up into a drop. Platforms text: a system tailored to your company, automating as much as possible and simplifying the rest. PWA text: anything built for the web, installable like any other app (no stores or their fees, one codebase, updates everywhere at once, less to spend). Print Design is Printing (Print With Us); Product Launch Campaigns is Launch Campaigns (chip Launch Campaign). Contact: heading and direct email over a wide two-column form. Footer: four columns, a legal row, a bottom row with the copyright and Back to top. Components state their own alignment (the site centers boxes by default). consent-web-library ^0.3.1
- 0.32.0: About (component/about, content/about) replaces Statement and Touchpoint ("One System", both removed): the sentence lighting up on scroll (your brand everywhere online, and the system that runs your business behind it), then the brand online (a numbered list) beside the platform that runs the business (automated, simple, anywhere) with a live feed ticking events in while the place it's viewed from changes. SECTION.about replaces SECTION.touchpoints in navigation, footer and indicator. Services title: "Pick where to start." Section ids: #about, #web, #desktop-and-mobile, #creative, #marketing (service group keys web and desktop-and-mobile). Capabilities: longer lists in every column (Web adds custom business management systems, AI search optimization, AI assistants and automations, payments, integrations, languages, analytics, domains and security, privacy and accessibility) and an Always Included row (icon-web-library ^0.3.0 check). Process: each dot lights when the line reaches it (process/measure-stops); on phones the line grows from the top. Hero leaves room for the service index on wide screens. - 0.33.0: About: the platform is also for teams who work by hand. Its text covers the office to the warehouse floor, with jobs reaching people as tasks on their phone; the points are Automated, Your team and Anywhere. The feed mixes the platform's own events with people's ("John packed the order", "Mary loaded the van", shown by their initial) and is headed Live. The brand panel has its own Brand label. ServiceUnlisted is no longer inside Services: it's a section of its own (h2), placed by the page after the capabilities. New Faq (component/faq, content/faq, SECTION.faq "Questions", #faq): ten questions in native details that ease open, a sticky heading with Ask Us, and FAQPage JSON-LD rendered with it (only on the page that shows it). In navigation, indicator and footer. Always Included: domain, hosting and accounts taken care of (or in your name), and everything legal done as the law requires. The footer's legal row is centered. Eyebrow states its alignment (starts on the left). Page order: hero, service index, about, services, capabilities, unlisted, marquee, process, faq, contact
- 0.34.0: Section indicator mirrored, in the margin right of the frame (from just past its line to the window's edge): the rail along the line; per row a tick in a fixed 34px slot (so nothing shifts when the section changes), the number, and the name to the right, ending at the window's edge when it doesn't fit ("safe" alignment, right to left). Smaller name pills in a narrower margin (container query); no pills where even those can't fit (the link's title names it). Capabilities: column headings stick under the bar; shorter columns run on in empty ruled cells (hidden on phones). Footer: Back to top under the style switch; the legal row (centered) starts with the copyright; no bottom row. FAQ: the legal answer says every country has its own rules, and that we find out what's mandatory wherever the client does business

- 0.36.0: Contact emails (form-web-library ^0.4.1): from "Sharadox Web Application" (CONTACT.sender "Sharadox"), subject "Sharadox Web Application · Contact · Name (Company)", the logo (content/email-logo EMAIL_LOGO, the app icon as base64 since 0.36.1) on black at the top, every detail, the message, then the form's page (hidden "page" field, location.href), language, time and IP; visitors who left an email get an automatic reply in English or Portuguese (CONTACT.acknowledgement) with their message, replying to which reaches contact@sharadox.com.
